name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: After the Attacker Leaves: Benchmarking Carryover Attacks on LLM Agents
items.dek: Benchmark shows prompt-injected payloads persist across agent sessions without decay; 101 attack tasks across five frontier models.
items.unproven: Tested on simulated scenarios; transfer to production agent workloads and real memory/task architectures unconfirmed.

items.title: AutoRedClaw: Automated Red-Teaming for Claw-Style Agents
items.dek: AutoRedClaw generates end-to-end attacks on persistent agent systems with poisoned configuration files and memory; execution-based validation ensures realism.
items.unproven: Evaluated on internal agents; attack success rates and coverage metrics on production claw-style systems not disclosed; generalization to other agent architectures unclear.

items.title: Proof-Carrying Contracts: Commitments AI Agents Cannot Break
items.dek: Framework enforces agent compliance to contract terms via machine-checkable proofs before execution, eliminating need to trust agent internals.
items.unproven: No deployed implementation; unclear how proof generation scales with agent complexity or real policy sets.

items.title: Disclosure Begets Disclosure: A Self-Reinforcing Privacy Loop in LLM Agents with Persistent Memory
items.dek: Multi-session simulation shows persistent LLM agent memory causes self-reinforcing privacy leakage loop; attribute inference margin widens over time.
items.unproven: Simulated users and four support models; transfer to real user behavior and production agent memory architectures not established.

items.title: EMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
items.dek: EMudhra intermediate CA certificate compromised; audit trust store, revocation status, and re-issuance for dependent systems.
items.unproven: scope of compromised certificate lineage, which end-entity certificates are affected, whether private key was extracted

items.title: ClawMMU: Protection-Coherent Virtual Memory for Stateful LLM Agents
items.dek: Protection layer tracks memory origin and authority to block indirect prompt injection; authority never self-elevates.
items.unproven: Conceptual design; no implementation, performance benchmarks, or integration path with existing agent frameworks provided.

items.title: Testing TLS 1.3 PQC on constrained devices and microcontrollers
items.dek: Post-quantum TLS 1.3 on microcontrollers: ML-KEM-512 + ML-DSA-44 handshakes 41% faster than X25519 + RSA-PSS on Pico W, contradicting assumption that lattice key exchange costs more.
items.unproven: Single-implementation benchmark (wolfSSL); no variation across TLS stacks, compilers, or optimization levels; interoperability and real-world deployment readiness unaddressed.

items.title: Local Allow, Global Deny: Why Per-Action Authorization Does Not Compose in LLM Agents
items.dek: Per-action authorization in LLM agents cannot enforce relational policies; compositional failures occur in 19.2% of test trajectories without cross-execution monitoring.
items.unproven: whether the theoretical impossibility result generalizes beyond the nine judges tested or translates to guardrail design constraints applicable to production agents.

items.title: Act on Your Behalf, Beyond Your Authorization: Benchmarking LLM Agent Authorization Alignment
items.dek: AuthorizationBench finds 19.2% of agent actions violate granted authorization across 6,864 trajectories; reasoning effort does not reduce violations.
items.unproven: whether results hold for agents with explicit authorization APIs or guardrails beyond the three harnesses tested; generalization to production delegation patterns.

items.title: Global Security Blind Spots: Translation as a Safety Bypass in Low-Resource Languages
items.dek: LLM safety alignment fails in 79 low-resource languages at 21.9–44.4% bypass rates despite English safety; risk concentrates in language families.
items.unproven: Does not establish whether model retraining on low-resource languages would close gaps; reflects translation quality confounds not fully separated.

items.title: You Are the Trigger: Speaker-Activated Backdoors
items.dek: Speaker-Activated Backdoor achieves 90–97% success on Whisper and Parakeet with two minutes of target audio; no inference-time trigger required.
items.unproven: Evaluated on fine-tuning threat model only; does not establish robustness to voice transformation, speaker variation, or deployed ASR quality; generalization to other speech models limited.

items.title: Energy Consumption of Post-Quantum Cryptography on Constrained and General-Purpose Architectures
items.dek: NIST post-quantum algorithms ML-KEM and ML-DSA match elliptic-curve efficiency; SLH-DSA signing costs 243% more energy on 32-bit IoT hardware and is impractical.
items.unproven: Tested on Raspberry Pi only; results may not generalize to other constrained architectures or custom silicon deployments.

items.title: The Internet goes on high alert after discovery of 8 compromised TLS certs
items.dek: Eight TLS certificates compromised; audit certificate pinning and CA trust policies, verify issuer controls.
items.unproven: scope of compromise, whether certificates were issued legitimately or through key extraction, remediation timeline

items.title: SPECTER: Covert Data Exfiltration from Air-Gapped Systems via USB Power Modulation
items.dek: Covert channel exfiltrates data from air-gapped systems by modulating USB power signals at 0.2–1.0 bit/sec; requires admin privileges.
items.unproven: Laboratory demonstration on two OS versions; applicability to hardened production environments and realistic secret sizes not established.

items.title: MAS-Guard: Unified Guardrails from Individual Agents to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.dek: Unified guardrail framework for single and multi-agent LLM systems combines local task experts, semantic checks, and deterministic structural controls.
items.unproven: Prototype framework; no field deployment data or head-to-head comparison with production agent safeguarding tooling.

items.title: Context-Aware Prompt Injection Detection via Small Language Models in RAG Pipelines: nokast-secureRAG
items.dek: 0.5B-parameter semantic firewall detects indirect prompt injection in RAG pipelines with 0.994 recall and 0.026 false-positive rate.
items.unproven: Held-out test set only; generalization to unseen attack families, real deployment latency, and integration with production RAG tooling unproven.

items.title: Contextual Candour: Role-Aware Graduated Disclosure for LLMs over Mixed-Sensitivity Contexts
items.dek: Graduated disclosure framework calibrates LLM response detail to user authorization level rather than binary grant-deny, reducing leakage on enterprise and clinical benchmarks.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to two benchmark domains; no evidence the approach scales to production agent-in-SDLC workflows or survives adversarial prompt injection at authorization boundaries.

items.title: Execution-Time Validation of Context-Carrying Action Intents in Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems
items.dek: Action Intent Schema formalizes the execution gap in cyber-physical systems and closes it with version-conditional commands, eliminating unprotected intervals in controlled ablations.
items.unproven: Limited to emulated and small-scale physical testbeds; no deployment evidence in production industrial cells or against realistic failure modes and operator workflows.

items.title: A Unified Attack Framework against Statistical Generative Watermarks for Large Language Models
items.dek: Black-box attack defeats seven LLM watermarking schemes by exploiting score-ratio alignment; detection rates drop to 0.05.
items.unproven: whether the attack transfers to production watermarking deployments with additional defenses or detection pipelines beyond the tested schemes.

noise.title: Google Cloud outage affects almost all banking and other operations in Europe
noise.dek: Google Cloud infrastructure failure across Europe; incident response and status tracking in real time.
noise.unproven: outside the reader's remit—this is operational incident response and infrastructure management, not application security engineering or SDLC governance.

noise.title: Google open-sources TorchTPU, a native PyTorch back end for TPUs
noise.dek: Google releases TorchTPU backend; infrastructure tooling, not application security or SDLC process.

noise.title: Mercury 3: Diffusion at scale
noise.dek: Mercury 3 diffusion model from commercial vendor; marketing for a product.
noise.unproven: whether claims hold outside vendor benchmarks or differ meaningfully from prior releases
